svg.text: Phase 2 — training the Siamese change detector
recall-first by design: the output is a ranked candidate list for human follow-up, not a final verdict
Setup
Encoder frozen (linear-probe regime) — only the change head is trained
Real same-object pairs only: 3,969 train pairs, ~13% positive
Binary focal loss (α 0.5, γ 2) · AdamW + cosine · head LR 1e-3 · 40 epochs
Head bias initialised to the observed positive rate → calibrated at step 0
Why freeze: 515 positives cannot support fine-tuning the whole backbone
without re-learning survey-specific shortcuts
Batch composition
WeightedRandomSampler with replacement → ~30% positives per batch
Sampling probabilities, not loss weights: batches really do contain ~19/64
positive pairs, with positives repeated across the epoch
Positive mass split equally across surveys: the 81 SDSS-V positives
get the same exposure as the 434 DESI ones
Epoch length = dataset size — no negative is discarded
Checkpoint selection
Metric: mean per-survey PR-AUC on validation
Each survey weighted equally, so the larger DESI arm cannot mask a
collapse on the science target (SDSS-V)
Not accuracy, not val loss: with a 13% positive rate both are dominated
by negatives, while PR-AUC measures the ranking we actually deploy
Operating threshold
Rule: maximum recall subject to FPR ≤ 5%, measured on the SDSS-V
validation subset — recall is optimised, FPR is only capped
The 5% cap is an inspection budget: how many false candidates a human
is willing to vet per batch of spectra, not a statistical criterion
F₂ sweep (recall weighted 2× precision) logged alongside as a diagnostic
Discipline
The threshold is fixed on validation and applied to the held-out test unchanged — it is never tuned on the test set. It is a
deployment parameter: on a new survey it is re-tuned to whatever inspection budget is available, without retraining the model.
